_note: Sample question bank for Showoff. Ten questions, spread across arena tiers. Schema derived from the Game UI page: a setup line carrying the game's voice, the question, four options, the answer, and the fact shown after the reveal (the 💡 line seen on 6.03/6.04). Arena is the difficulty tier, on the assumption that A1 is easiest and A6 hardest — 'The guessing stops working here' appears on a later arena. Confirm that assumption before building on it.

questions.setup: Everyone says Sydney. Everyone is wrong.
questions.question: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.fact: Canberra exists because Sydney and Melbourne couldn't stop arguing. They built a whole city in the gap between them.

questions.question: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.fact: Two pump blood to the gills, one to the rest of the body. That third one stops beating when they swim, which is why they'd rather walk.

questions.setup: Closest to the sun. Not the hottest. Deal with it.
questions.question: Which planet has the hottest surface?
questions.fact: Venus sits at about 465°C — hot enough to melt lead — because its atmosphere traps heat that Mercury simply radiates away.

questions.question: What colour is a polar bear's skin?
questions.fact: The fur isn't white either — it's translucent and hollow. The bear just scatters light very convincingly.

questions.setup: The name is doing a lot of work here.
questions.question: How long did the Hundred Years' War actually last?
questions.fact: 1337 to 1453. Nobody called it that at the time — the name was applied centuries later, by people who didn't count.

questions.question: Which of these is botanically a berry?
questions.fact: A berry grows from a single ovary with seeds inside. Strawberries fail on every count — those aren't even seeds on the outside.

questions.question: What is the largest desert on Earth?
questions.fact: A desert is defined by how little falls out of the sky, not by temperature. Antarctica is about 14 million km² of it.

questions.setup: Russia has eleven. Russia is not the answer.
questions.question: Which country spans the most time zones?
questions.fact: France reaches twelve, thanks to overseas territories scattered across every ocean. China spans five geographically and insists on using one.

questions.setup: Take a second with this one. You'll need it.
questions.question: Which came first — the fax machine or the American Civil War?
questions.fact: Alexander Bain patented it in 1843, eighteen years before Fort Sumter. The technology sat around waiting for a purpose for over a century.

questions.question: Cleopatra lived closer in time to which of these?
questions.fact: The Great Pyramid was already 2,500 years old when she was born. The Moon landing was only 2,000 years after she died.
